posts.content_html_raw:
A trivial Io question that I haven't really understood: (Nonetheless, I'm Here)




When Sensei approached Io with questions related to her past, she dodged, reasonably so. But after some exchanges, Io went back to her cop-out answer and said things like "my cop-out answer is not in the way you might be expecting". What does that mean? Sensei pondered on her original answer and got confused even more when Io threw this extra metaphor, forcing him to dig through his brain to only end with his own generic cop-out answer and give up early.

At this point much of Io's unfortunate circumstances have been revealed, and it's almost certain that it'd be related to either her medication history or her sexually abusive mother. But, I still can't really tell what exactly she was referring to. What is the hidden layer underneath “I really did just wake up and walk to the bathhouse”? Wake up from a horrible nightmare? A medication-induced dizziness? Or is it the Walk part that requires some imaginations?

If I picture this in a more heart-wrenching way, I might guess that wizard Io maybe really did just wake up and walk here, one day deciding to run away and seek shelter. Or worse, she just aimlessly wandered around the streets in her broken state and, luckily enough, wandered into her aunt’s lair. It might happen when the border closed, or right before that. Either way, I feel like this is too literal to be referred to as a metaphor, so I’m wondering if this is in fact already hinted elsewhere.

I'm sorry that other people have reacted negatively to your opinion on this game. On another post, you said you want to stick around. So if you don't mind, i want to share my experience with this game with you. It may also explain why other commenters feel strongly about your opinions.
When i first played this game 2 years ago, i didn't enjoy it much either, for similar reasons. What was there to enjoy? There were not many sexy scenes, and they were not sexy. There were a few "scary scenes" that didn't scare me. One dimensional characters who already in love wih mc. So as a player i couldn't even witness that bonding over time. At the beginning, game literally says none of the things you will see is real. Why would i take anything serious after this point, if it is all a dream.

So what did i do? shift+deleted the lessons in love file and forgot about it...

One year later, i stumbled upon this game again. Realised, i already played it and didn't liked it. After all it was a shitty game. But i was bored at the time and already jerked off to eternum. So why not give it another chance at this non sexual porn game.

Playing this game without any sexual expectation or desire was an experience.

The game that explicitly told me nothing is real and i shouldn't take it serious made me laugh, angry, think, frustrated, excited, surprised, sad, determined.

The no reason to progress girls that already head over heels for mc, they were funny, loveable, hateable, compassionate,selfish. I laughed at them, i felt sad for them, i cared about them, i was scared for them, i was scared of them.

And it all happened in a organic way, that i didn't expect from this game.


Other people will say "if you are here for porn, go away. This game is not for you" and i agree with them. This game is not for everyone, but it could be the just right game for you. In a different time and a state of mind, give this game another chance. Because i'm glad that i did.




PS: Use AutoVN mod to get rid of both grinding affection points, and figuring out event triggers.

Sensei pondered on her original answer and got confused even more when Io threw this extra metaphor, forcing him to dig through his brain to only end with his own generic cop-out answer and give up early.

Or worse, she just aimlessly wandered around the streets in her broken state and, luckily enough, wandered into her aunt’s lair. It might happen when the border closed, or right before that. Why are we getting called Sekai during happy events?
Click to expand...
Hasn't been confirmed. Since I don't know how far into the game you are, beware the speculation below. Theories are as such:
1. Akira is Sekai in a traumatic sense.
2. Akira is with Sekai in a paranormal sense.
3. Akira is with Sekai in a psychological sense.

We have seen Sekai with Akira a number of times. Both as his shadow (in the early game), as in his flashback triggered from Niki's letters, possibly in Yasu's monologue to him in "Frankincense" (about the one that follows him, although that may not be Sekai), but, most important of all, through many dialogues that state that Sekai is bound to him as a lifeline to not disappear.
Sekai is his shadow.
Thus, in that sense, he sort of is Sekai. It is also possible that he actually is Sekai in a more Sekaori kind of way. One option for that would be that he's playing out Sekai's original role. Thus, Akira is the player occupying the position that should have been Sekai's in 23. That would explain why Am I Okay addresses him as such, especially at a time when "Akira" wasn't as aware of who he was.

A number of recent events hint at that possibility. Akira's home is not 23, but 22. Both Sekai and Akira are children of Yuu (the previous protagonist), and thus capable of carrying his "legacy/curse". We infer that Sekai had been prepared to serve as a hotel for gods, which, ultimately, ended up with Kaori being cursed with that job since she took in what remained of Sekai. This puts both of them in a similar situation in relation to the gods and the overall grand scheme of things.

Finally, this relationship has been revisited both in Maki's last event (where Sekai seems to be a figment of Akira's imagination) - and, at the same time, a possible unwilling participant in his infection by her "bad" parts (the real Sekai that is) - as seen in Karin's event "Uzbekistan".
It seems like a worm was implanted into Sekai and it's not helping her in her objective. She's then desperate to not let the worm reach Akira, but seems to fail to do so.

Why are we getting called Sekai during happy events?
Click to expand...
Hasn't been confirmed. Since I don't know how far into the game you are, beware the speculation below. Theories are as such:
Spoiler:
speculation
1. Akira is Sekai in a traumatic sense.
2. Akira is with Sekai in a paranormal sense.
3. Akira is with Sekai in a psychological sense.
We have seen Sekai with Akira a number of times. Both as his shadow (in the early game), as in his flashback triggered from Niki's letters, possibly in Yasu's monologue to him in "Frankincense" (about the one that follows him, although that may not be Sekai), but, most important of all, through many dialogues that state that Sekai is bound to him as a lifeline to not disappear.
Spoiler:
Spotless mind
Sekai is his shadow.
Thus, in that sense, he sort of is Sekai. It is also possible that he actually is Sekai in a more Sekaori kind of way. One option for that would be that he's playing out Sekai's original role. Thus, Akira is the player occupying the position that should have been Sekai's in 23. That would explain why Am I Okay addresses him as such, especially at a time when "Akira" wasn't as aware of who he was.
A number of recent events hint at that possibility. Akira's home is not 23, but 22. Both Sekai and Akira are children of Yuu (the previous protagonist), and thus capable of carrying his "legacy/curse". We infer that Sekai had been prepared to serve as a hotel for gods, which, ultimately, ended up with Kaori being cursed with that job since she took in what remained of Sekai. This puts both of them in a similar situation in relation to the gods and the overall grand scheme of things.
Finally, this relationship has been revisited both in Maki's last event (where Sekai seems to be a figment of Akira's imagination) - and, at the same time, a possible unwilling participant in his infection by her "bad" parts (the real Sekai that is) - as seen in Karin's event "Uzbekistan".
Spoiler:
Hello alone
Spoiler:
A trip to Uzbekistan
It seems like a worm was implanted into Sekai and it's not helping her in her objective. She's then desperate to not let the worm reach Akira, but seems to fail to do so.
Edit: Added screenshots.
Bingoogus said:
i went and replayed the theme hospital scene again... man does it pay-off after stomachache.
Click to expand...
I highly recommend you take a look at the care package about Io's future through text messages. It explores a lot about how she feels about being "assexual" through trauma, and how she's been working and keeps working to overcome it. I thought it was really heartwarming. There's also some funny bits about how
she built a chair, and calls it the cuck chair, because she forces herself to sit and watch Akira having sex with Uta
in an effort to desensitize herself

More of the narration:
I think this has to be Narrator Ami speaking. We know that Ami is infected with a worm that she wants to get rid of ("Della") and unlike Sekai she still has a body (present tense) for the worm to have been put into. In other events, she consistently narrates with poetry which has weird typography and/or abruptly cuts off due to her increasing madness. The narrator connects the negative of her worm with the positive of a "gift," and we know Ami's infection came with at least one gift: her skill at poetry.

Here's another event where Narrator Ami talks about how her mind is rotting, she's going mad, and she's afraid of doing something that inadvertently harms Akira.


Narrator Ami is the girl with broken wings - currently, she can't fly.

These lines probably have multiple meanings, but literally they describe how Maya is knocking on Ami's door before letting herself in.
It's possible that "Narrator Ami" was originally some version of Sekai (among other things she addresses her poems to "Boy"), but the important thing is that at this point she's narrating from Ami Arakawa's perspective (even saying "I am Ami" in "Wake Up (My Story)"), so the infection/worm in "A Trip to Uzbekistan" is the same one Ami talks about in "Della."

Biology adapts to achieve it's goals and sometimes it's a little too good at it.

It definitely took a whole journey for me to get over the feeling of "I don't deserve love, anyone who likes me would be a weirdo" but I did it. And I can now empathize with the opposite sex as well because petite women DO exist and they also have to deal with that sort of insecurity too, even if it is a bit less socially intense than it is for a guy.

Of course that being said, I personally can find beauty all shapes of the female form and have been fortunate to have some generally successful relationships that I cherished with women that were bigger/taller than me. That in particular is something that I actually appreciate greatly with LiL's handling of realistic proportions.

Futaba might not be one of the best characters in the story admittedly, but I respect that Sel was willing to include an overweight girl and attempt to flesh her out even if her story still needs some more attention, and I empathize with Molly and her insecurities with her underdeveloped body since I went through a similar thing in my youth.

The characters are good man.

The fourth mind:

- "One last element. One last mind. Again, unnoticed."
- "Important note: when did she even get here?"
- "Four people, four minds. Now turn them into atoms and stack them on top of each other. Watch them tunnel like worms, not deer (me). Or ants, not deer (you)."
('Il Cervo' Commentary)
Probably, the way it was framed is important as well. Kaori the game master. Ami the player before the event. Sensei the last to join. And the 4th that was unnoticed.

Even in a world where the Io thing didn't happen, the way the girls act in Nodokathon is nonsensical. These are teenagers who have had at most one sexual partner. Just because they're horny perverts doesn't mean they're going to jump at the chance to get naked and pleasure themselves in front of a random group of their classmates, not all of whom are their friends.

Even before the girls witnessed Nodoka reveal Io's most intimate secret, they already knew that she's the creepy incest girl who has zero respect for other people's personal boundaries. With the possible exception of Rin, none of them are friends with her. And yet they decided to accept her vague invitation to some sexual event, without knowing the specifics of what they would have to do or who else would even show up (for the most part).

All of the girls have individual factors that should prevent them from participating:
  • Rin knows Nodoka is writing a book about their sex lives and is constantly manipulating others, she knows this shit isn't going to stay private. She also gets extremely embarrassed and stops functioning in any situation that's even remotely sexual.
  • Makoto is in her "doesn't give a fuck" phase and has no inhibitions, but she also has no incentive to participate - she's straight, so it doesn't do anything for her sexually. Her most notable previous interaction with Nodoka is being (repeatedly?) sexually assaulted by her in the gym showers. There's no chance she'd give Nodoka the satisfaction of agreeing to what she wants.
  • Sana is a secret degenerate, but she's also cripplingly shy and has only just started to come out of her shell. It's insane that she would do something sexual with people that she still struggles to even have a conversation with.
  • Molly's degeneracy is limited to h-games that she plays in private because she's scared to get involved with real people.

  • Even Kirin's supposed promiscuity is all talk, no action. There's a reason she's never been with anyone other than Sensei.
We often say that LiL isn't a porn game, it just contains explicit scenes in service of telling a particular story. Nodokathon is porn for porn's sake and doesn't belong here. To make it happen Sel had to ignore consistent characterization in favor of ridiculous porn logic.

I can relate to that. But I don't think Nodokathon is merely a fan-service. Nodoka elaborated her intention in detail here.







As in, she's trying to "break character and shell of everything" to save everyone from given inertia and inanity. I believe in Chandler's Law she talked about same thing. Nodokathon is no exception, all part of her experiment to find more intriguing aspects of character to help her understand and distort the world.
Click to expand...
I found myself agreeing and disagreeing at the same time. Agreeing part is that Nodokathon didn’t happen without a deeper reason. I don’t really mind why those six girls showing up despite the very recent Io incident; some wouldn’t understand the full picture, some might not care at all, and most of them have personality weaknesses that could be easily tapped by Nodoka via invitations. They showed up for her experiment unbeknownst to them.

The disagreeing part is how poorly defined this experiment is, or how intentionally hidden an explanation is behind content wall higher than the walls surrounding Kumon-mi, to a point that believing her experiment becomes a tough pill to swallow. Saying this is because her experiment can be summed up to “rebelling against this strange world and understanding Kyoko’s words via all female sexual contests”. Like WHAT? How does that make any sense? How did she come to this conclusion that this particular experimental procedure might’ve brought the results she sought? It’s exactly 1-yr anniversary of Nodokathon and has she really learned anything from it? Has any participant become any “different” related to this purpose after Nodokathon? Did any potential insight provided by Nodokathon partially help her reach the roof? If yes then how? Does Makoto backing down or not affect her conclusion of this experiment? If no then why? Would you(Selly, not you) mind explaining how exactly Nodokathon could achieve Nodoka’s goal?
(If there actually is mention somewhere that indicates Nodoka learned something via Nodokathon pls slap right in my face; I’ve never stopped judging this event chain and I’d like to change that if possible)

I care less a lot why she does things and care a lot more how and why certain experiments can do just that. For this I have a million more questions for Nodokathon. But because I have not been convinced that Selly/Nodoka can answer them properly and Nodokathon itself doesn’t seem to really on-screen help Nodoka become one step closer to her goal, I have no reason to believe this isn’t just a mindless fan service and it’s no wonder that many of us think Nodokathon is just that. Let’s face it, THAT is what we received and you’ve really gotta just hardcore believe in Nodoka and Selly without a doubt to just buy everything Nodoka said that night as if Nodokathon was some secret villain plots that don’t need to make any sense to the audience (“it just is okay it makes perfect sense stop asking you don’t know shit” kinda deal). And this pisses me off to no end; it’s like Selly doesn’t know how to make Nodoka smart so he forces his audience to be stupid.

It may be my lack of sleep talking... but the more I play through the game, the more and more I start getting the "Coma" vibes with Sensei.

Specifically, I'm reminded of a pretty well known story of a redditor who, after being knocked unconscious, to the point that they nearly died; experienced an entire life while in that Coma/Unconscious state. In the story, the guy apparently lived several years (some argue as much as fifteen) in this parallel world.

posts.content_html_raw:
Yes, but I'd put that "Il Cervo" further points in the opposite direction.

As Selebus puts it, there is the actual plot and then there are certain events which are "experiments", things that didn't really happen, but act as narrative representations of feelings, emotions, a mind going through motions while sharing the same space with others.
On the event itself, "Il Cervo", rather, is the attempt from Selebus to instill narrative sense to something that is meaningless, while still communicating the message that it has no meaning. "Experiment" really is the best word for it, and as to which degree it was successful, I haven't made up my mind about it (after understanding it better).

"There was no game. There was no one there. They weren't talking to eachother, and everything you see is the reader trying to make sense of four minds joined together in an event for economy sake, but that actually were alone (just in the same geographic space more or less)." I mean, I saw absolutely no one that got this from that event.

I tend, currently, to think it failed - especially because if I have to reconsider everything I see as not only a possible hallucination on Akira's part, but on "my" (the reader)'s part, then we're all screwed. But I have to think about it some more.
In other words, that "Il Cervo" didn't happen, to me, means that the actual plot happens (as he has said so many times) - because "Il Cervo" is an exception.

posts.content_html_raw:
Honestly, I think people might be missing the point with Red Path Io and Green Path Io.

Red Path Io had her traumatized mentality shattered when a pedo that she trusted chose not to violate her. She didn't think this was possible, hence her later excessive lovey doveyness, and seeing Sensei like an angel:
Red Path Io - "Are you an angel?..."
(Chapter 4 'Empty Heart Appeal' Main Event)
He was a miracle from her point of view. He proved that there was hope for her. She wasn't just born to be a tool:
Red Path Io - "All of my life...I've been a tool."
- "Am I..."
- "Actually free now?"
(Chapter 4 'Empty Heart Appeal' Main Event)

Green Path Io had her beliefs confirmed. Sensei was a pedo that'd violate her, even while saying the exact same things that her mother, who violated her, did:
Green Path Io - "Mhm. It's easy when you use the same words she used to."
(Chapter 4 Io 'Stomachache' Event)
There isn't really any coming back from that. He cemented the reality she knew. There was no hope, just acceptance. She accepted her place:
Green Path Io - "This is what I was put here for."
- "And I'd much rather be your tool than anyone else's..."
(Chapter 4 Io 'Stomachache' Event)

Recently, it's got to a similar stage where in both paths; Sensei doesn't want to violate her. This, at best, gives Green Path Io some hope. (While for Red Path Io, he already chose not to. Now, he's chosen not to, twice. Further cementing who he is to her.)

However, if/when Sensei blacks out on her, or simply reaches his limit, Red Path Io will have reason to believe that he's truly not being himself. It's not entirely his fault. He isn't like that. He's already proved it.

On the other hand, Green Path Io will have reason to believe that of course he was all talk. He's just like the rest and he's only going to make excuses and black out, if she doesn't force herself to spread her legs to keep him around.

Overall: It probably doesn't really matter. Io is trapped, just like everyone else. A different flavor of text probably won't change the true end much, if at all.

Of course, Sel may have other plans.

Honestly, I think people might be missing the point with Red Path Io and Green Path Io.

Red Path Io had her traumatized mentality shattered when a pedo that she trusted chose not to violate her. She didn't think this was possible, hence her later excessive lovey doveyness, and seeing Sensei like an angel:
View attachment 4711641 Red Path Io - "Are you an angel?..."

View attachment 4711635 View attachment 4711637 View attachment 4711639 Red Path Io - "All of my life...I've been a tool."
- "Am I..."
- "Actually free now?"

Green Path Io had her beliefs confirmed. Sensei was a pedo that'd violate her, even while saying the exact same things that her mother, who violated her, did:
View attachment 4711660 Green Path Io - "Mhm. It's easy when you use the same words she used to."
(Chapter 4 Io 'Stomachache' Event)

View attachment 4711630 View attachment 4711631 Green Path Io - "This is what I was put here for."
- "And I'd much rather be your tool than anyone else's..."
(Chapter 4 Io 'Stomachache' Event)

However, if/when Sensei blacks out on her, or simply reaches his limit, Red Path Io will have reason to believe that he's truly not being himself. It's not entirely his fault. He isn't like that. He's already proved it.

On the other hand, Green Path Io will have reason to believe that of course he was all talk. He's just like the rest and he's only going to make excuses and black out, if she doesn't force herself to spread her legs to keep him around.

Overall: It probably doesn't really matter. Io is trapped, just like everyone else. A different flavor of text probably won't change the true end much, if at all.

Of course, Sel may have other plans.

This brings up something on my mind about Io’s red path: the current positivity there in red path is so much that I really cannot neglect it and directly claim that “green is still the path to eventual happiness for Io”. When people were praising green path Sensei for rejecting Io’s handjob, I kept thinking that 1) this merely means the merging of the two paths that subsequently reduces the impact of the Stomachache choice on their relationship, and 2) like you mentioned, hasn’t this difficult decision already been achieved by red path Sensei in a much larger scale a lot earlier??? This only proves that there is still hope for green path Sensei; this doesn’t automatically mean red path Sensei did anything wrong.

Granted, the mutual understanding and consensus made between Io and Sensei in these two paths are indeed significantly different; green path seems to offer higher chances of future consenting Io sex while red path kinda just embraces Io’s displayed asexuality. But that’s it. The potential lack of future consenting sex (which may not be true by the way) by itself in the red path is by no means something damning. What might be damning instead is in fact: 1) current Sensei will not be able to handle an asexual relationship, and 2) Selly might “punish” red path players with possibly blackout sex or other horrible things.

To me, reason1 is thinking way too far ahead while ignoring the remaining Sensei x Io journey that has yet to unveil, and reason2 is literally something we imagine to convince ourselves and scare everyone else who didn’t make the same choice as us (seriously, have we ever become good at predicting Sensei’s blackout sexual assault even?). Since there really isn’t any in-game indicator that implies the possibility of any planned misfortune for red path Io (an example of this would be “Pareidolia murmuring about punishing akira for disobeying the destroy her command”), I will continue to remain brazen until the day something does happen all because Sensei didn’t Stomachache Io or when Selly does dish out punishment; only then will I shit my pants and change my mind.



I said all that but I’m actually on green path But not because I think green would be better (in all definitions) for Sensei x Io in a long run, but because I simply fucking refuse to miss content.

I have to throw my hat in with those that view the green path as the true path to healing, at least in the context of this story. Stomachache is a fantastical, extreme depiction of two traumatized people sharing the absolute blackest pits of themselves with each other. Were it in real life, it would be a marathon of tears, old pictures, news articles and stories of every betrayal and disappointment they ever experienced. The night would end like passing out in a sauna filled with guilt and self-loathing. Sound familiar?

Green path allows her to indulge the hail-mary urge to take control of her self-perception as the abused by offering herself up as a sacrifice. In turn, Akira indulges his perception that abuse and corruption are an inevitable, self-perpetuating cycle that justifies itself as long as the encounters are pleasurable in the end. Both of them end up miserable. But, just like a bully and would-be victim that become best friends after brawling each other in a fit of immature rage, the fact they found someone that respects them after seeing them at their worst breaks all logic and fuses their damaged souls together for life. They've seen the bottom of the pit and together, writhed in the filth and bones of the memories that haunt their every day.

I'm sorry, but no amount of temporary pain can convince me to deny them this catharsis. They know if Akira wanted to take her, she would let him. They know that she would come running back to him even if he did so. And still, he chooses her happiness over his own pleasure, even when she tries to force the issue. "He will fill the pit with his pallid light no matter how deep we go. And the only place we have to go from here is up."

Red path shows the beginnings of an insidious, creeping anxiety. "If not now, when? I am the abused and he is the abuser. It will happen someday and the only question is how much will it hurt. And the more I trust this lie, the deeper the pain will be..." The key motif within the red path version of Even Winning Feels Bad is distance. "Guardian angel", "Am I really safe here?", the focus on the far future, and of course hiding or being unable to articulate her true feelings about her past and her non-existant sense of self-worth. A step backwards when we'd come so far towards connection. The blinding light of a biblically accurate Akira provides equal parts terror and salvation, as it rightly should.

Here's the thing, the actual decision to flip what the dialogue shows is simple af. amifingered = false and ami_virgin = true. If you just want to see alternate dialogue those two should give you everything you need.

But you're playing with a ticking time bomb if you try to cheat this midway through the game. Events are flagged as missing when they were implemented, so randomly in the code often in the events for other people, and in your case you'll have flags that say you haven't fucked ami but have seen events that require you to have fucked ami. This could be detected at any point Sel wants, and you'd just take whatever punishment he feels is right. None of us would even argue he'd be going too far, unlike making a cheat menu and then punishing you for using it. If something ever went wrong for doing this we'd have to remember you did this and not give you any help because of course things will break like this.

Just get URM, there's a link in Bingoogus's signature. You can use it to edit flags if you must, but what's probably the better option is viewing said events in replays. URM would let you see all potential dialogue choices, and if you're watching events in replays it should default to not fucking Ami outside of amifingered specific events.

posts.content_html_raw:
Antosha said:
Wow. Sure showed me.

Activist? Not trying to make anyone go with a different choice than they want to. And I played Stomachache. Not going to replay it, thanks.

Hurting people because you can't not hurt them--that I can go with. Most of the relationships in this game are complete train wrecks. The blackout with Yumi, etc., pissed me off, but those scenes told me about the character I was playing. Knowingly, actively hurting someone just because? Not my thing. I know he's an asshole. I know they're all completely fucked up.

But Sel gave us the choice in Stomachache for a reason (unlike most of those earlier scenes). So I rolled back and took it. And I'll change the flag with URM when there's a reason to. But for now? I'm happy with my choice.

The only other choice I really had to think about not rolling back was the one in the shower with Yumi and Nodoka. I didn't roll back and take the red path there, though it left a really awful taste in my mouth. Still does. But I honestly felt as if that choice fit Akira at that point -- taking the path of least resistance, which coincidentally got him an HJ and an eyeful of Yumi, which seemed like things he'd really like.

In Stomachache? He's actively trying to Do the Right Thing, something he's been working at since the previous reset. It's not a huge jump for me to think that it's easier for NOT to fuck Io.
Click to expand...
I understand this post comes from a place of defense, so I'll not overly address its tone - just a few points:
1. Akira definitely doesn't engage in stomachache "just because". He tries to use his tools for "good" and is confronted with them not working in the most horrible manner, which teaches him a harsh reality about himself and what was done to him - as well as what kind of relationship he wants with Io (not because he's a saint), but because he'd rather never experience "stomachache" again - which is far more believable.

I believe Akira to be able to control himself because he's experienced stomachache, he knows what that will look like with Io, thus he chooses the path of least resistance: not having anything sexual with her ever again. The red path is, as it has been eloquently put by previous posts, iffy at best and full of anxiety.

Or, if by "just because" you mean the player choosing just because, well, one would choose to see the actual story, it wouldn't be without reason.

2. "Matador" and "Stomachache" do not equate. To "choose" whether Yumi falls to blackmail or not is a metagaming move. In Rin's good/bad homie, you could say "well, even though the game doesn't give you a choice menu, Rin does tell you to avoid Chika and the player can go from there". But to avoid "Matador", you have to not see "Abyss" before the Onsen trip, and how does that translate into "yeah, I chose for Yumi to fall to blackmail"?

Imo, and Selebus' (since I was outed as his personal friend), the choice that you are given in Stomachache is to further reinforce being part of this. It's a situation of "how can I make this hit even harder? Well, give the player an explicit choice of being able to walk away or see the event." I have said this before, but the choices that are given in this game are garbage.

I wouldn't suggest reading much into it because there's no greater plan in that regard. Selebus has said so (seriously this time). My take is that the choice in stomachache is an experiment that worked out great, and that has been resolved already. There are simply too many characters and plotlines for it to matter much more than that, and far too few choices (as of right now) for it to trigger a "you're too weak" onto the player (although it has been hinted already with the Chinami shower event").
All of this being said, my main save is green, and so is all of my replay, save for stomachache. It's very emotionally taxing, and for all my praise for it, I'm not replaying it more than necessary (I've already talked about it a lot, and have probably watched it far more than the average player).

Thus I think people should also think about why people are skipping it and cut them some slack. It's a very particular group of people that are drawn to LiL, and we don't know if/what part of their lives resonates with which event.
Edit: I've written many posts about "stomachache" already, so I recommend them if anyone is looking for a more in-depth analysis - this one isn't it.

shmurfer said:
Here's the thing, the actual decision to flip what the dialogue shows is simple af. amifingered = false and ami_virgin = true. If you just want to see alternate dialogue those two should give you everything you need.

But you're playing with a ticking time bomb if you try to cheat this midway through the game. Events are flagged as missing when they were implemented, so randomly in the code often in the events for other people, and in your case you'll have flags that say you haven't fucked ami but have seen events that require you to have fucked ami. This could be detected at any point Sel wants, and you'd just take whatever punishment he feels is right. None of us would even argue he'd be going too far, unlike making a cheat menu and then punishing you for using it. If something ever went wrong for doing this we'd have to remember you did this and not give you any help because of course things will break like this.

Just get URM, there's a link in Bingoogus's signature. You can use it to edit flags if you must, but what's probably the better option is viewing said events in replays. URM would let you see all potential dialogue choices, and if you're watching events in replays it should default to not fucking Ami outside of amifingered specific events.

I don't really have any objections to what you're saying here. It's all well thought out and very reasonable for the perspectives it explores. The viewer and Sensei all have plenty of reason to think the red path is better for everyone. But that's the point isn't it?

Io's presence in the story has been dedicated to setting her up as a walking, breathing contradiction. Someone that desires to just be close with someone but her every action is an invitation to hurt her instead. Betraying that theming now would be a level of literary incompentence nearly impossible given the track record of the rest of the work. There's three layers that do the heavy lifting for me on green path being better for Io:

1. Io's character being centered around refusing to connect with anyone and the immense weight of what she committed to do in order to attempt connection.
2. The Chekhov's gun factor of teaching us how hard it is for Io to hide her emotions and general zeal for cold hard truth.
3. The meta layer of green path using a clash of expectations and genuine surprise to set up a revelation payoff while red path focuses on doubt and frailty to set the stage for deep betrayal.

Before we proceed, healing to me is about mastering your own self-perception and overcoming the emotional control previous trauma has on you. Thanks to her role as a character in a drama, the path she takes to get there must be appropriately dramatic. So given the two options of path, let's give an example outline of what I consider to be the most likely dramatic payoffs of each path.

Green.1: Sensei controls himself and their bond slowly matures into something they both enjoy, which may or may not contain sex or threesomes. (tension of will they/won't they, payoff for braving the darkness, self-actualizaiton if the threesome comes about... Polycule with one Ace in the mix?... Whatever, anyway.)

Green.2: Sensei goes HAPPY at some point and Io weathers the storm with empathy, having already faced this particular darkness and coming to accept her own commitment to being what he needs her to be. (role reversal, empowerment, wielding the callouses of trauma to your advantage for the sake of another)

Red.1: Sensei controls himself forever, making it challenging to meaningfully write her into a scenario where she faces her trauma again. Io either never gets over her fear and doubt (stagnates character development), she slowly unravels and perhaps eventually forces herself on him in some way (traumatizing them both) or somehow finds a way to overcome trauma without facing it (contrived and undramatic OR sappy, rom-com style deference of her character to a savior). The threesome makes no sense to come about in this path because it contradicts the idea that he can truly invest in a relationship without sex being involved. (She becomes a person that only exists by the grace of someone else crafting a world for her.)

Red.2: Sensei goes HAPPY at some point and Io learns that the only thing that made things bearable in the past was the darkness itself. Every fear and doubt she has for the world and her future is validated by the betrayal of the first person she allowed herself to trust, whether she was lying to herself or not.

The issue here is that in this story and it's metaphysical tug-of-war, ain't nobody gonna sit through years of therapy and get a healthy father figure and self-actualize through hobbies or careers and move out and become their own person and slowly grow beyond their past. Of course on paper, red path would be the right path for someone in her position. It sets her up to do the above provided that the environment she's in could supply that experience.

It can't and it won't.

Kumon-mi is among the worst case scenarios for someone that needs to move on. They are literally denied the very concept of self-improvement and growth over time. What little they have access to comes exclusively at the hands of a little toy man being cast about by a clash of wills. You must be able to stand on your own two feet to survive the barriers to growth in this place.

Think about the counterfactuals when you choose your path. Think about what payoff the storytellers of this world will be able to get in each scenario. By crashing to the bottom right away, you force the storytellers hand and increase her chances of a happy ending. If instead you deny her agency, you simply paint a target on her back and set her up to remain a puppet.

Someone that desires to just be close with someone but her every action is an invitation to hurt her instead. Betraying that theming now would be a level of literary incompentence nearly impossible given the track record of the rest of the work. There's three layers that do the heavy lifting for me on green path being better for Io:
Spoiler:
Genre savvy is a hell of a drug

Before we proceed, healing to me is about mastering your own self-perception and overcoming the emotional control previous trauma has on you. Thanks to her role as a character in a drama, the path she takes to get there must be appropriately dramatic. Green.1: Sensei controls himself and their bond slowly matures into something they both enjoy, which may or may not contain sex or threesomes. (tension of will they/won't they, payoff for braving the darkness, self-actualizaiton if the threesome comes about... Polycule with one Ace in the mix?... Whatever, anyway.)
Green.2: Sensei goes HAPPY at some point and Io weathers the storm with empathy, having already faced this particular darkness and coming to accept her own commitment to being what he needs her to be. (role reversal, empowerment, wielding the callouses of trauma to your advantage for the sake of another)
Red.1: Sensei controls himself forever, making it challenging to meaningfully write her into a scenario where she faces her trauma again. must

Tbh I feel like you are having too much of a negative bias towards the outcomes of red path as a result of the story rarely allowing positive outcomes. You keep mentioning her fear, doubt, and frailty. I'm not denying that the possibility of a false hope is definitely there (and likely even) or that those characteristics aren't a core part of her personality deep down, but Io herself does not display these emotions any more than normal during the events following compared to green path. As a matter of fact, in red path she displays positivity and hope. This is the first time we've seen her in game take a single step toward the direction of "wait, maybe I'm not 100% trash... I might only be 90%" and actually seem...almost happy for once. Obviously this could very well end up turning on its head but from what we get in game red path doesn't directly allude to her being any more frail or scared. It's not something that we can see working out from what the story has given us thus far because barely anything really has before. But we know already that theoretically it eventually WILL happen with the purity routes.

That being said, it seems like that kind of meta-narrative shift is still a ways off. So the likelihood of an actual positive outcome like this is pretty low at this point, I do agree. However like I've said before, I just can't help but latch on to that idealized fantasy of giving her just a slice of hope and reassurance. I don't care if Selebus makes me regret it, I want so badly for this moment to be real for her. I will accept the consequences if it does end up backfiring and despair accordingly. The meaning of this story to me is to be able to face all of the struggles and tragedies this world has to offer and yet still continue to HOPE and see the beauty and light that exists in the vast sea of darkness.




Also, it's not like Akira is pretending that the possibility of him hurting her doesn't exist and he's somehow a good person suddenly after refusing to assault her "one time". He makes it clear that he still has problems and that there's always a risk. Some may argue that she will inevitably begin to trust him more and more until he breaks it catastrophically, but I personally feel like she's smart and self-aware enough to realize the fallacy.



There is a chance that he could black out on red path and she still finds the will to sympathize and still connect with him through it. I'm actually not sure if it would be more cathartic for her to have experienced something similar with him already and being more prepared for it, or her proving her love for him is more than just based on an idealized version of him by dealing with it out of the blue and still finding the will to carry on. I think the latter would actually elevate my opinion of her character even more.


The way he uniquely asks for her hand verbally in red path tells its own story.

In conclusion,
Io cute.

posts.content_html_raw:
It's nice that the game is complex and thus allows complex opinions and complex reasonings, it's a pleasure for me to read them.
Though I haven't been present here while og Stomachache discussion or even read it, I have a smol reasoning to share as it was my first post about it here and having looked at bigger and deeper things about the game for awhile my vision of it haven't faded.
So, green Stomachache is a good player's trap.
Sel is an author of specific disposition toward players.
Thus, looking at the event a bit wider than characters and plot, the player's decision is of meaning and of assessment. Green is good? Yep, tons of justifications for it. But as for motivation behind this decision - it's compliance (with the plot, 'characters growth', 'greenness line' etc.), could even be assessed the same as local title of lilcordians' - sycophancy towards the author, the plotbearer. So, yes - going green is going canon, going right, going good. And as of the whole community - yes, of course. But personally? It's like differences between Western (primacy of person) and Eastern (primacy of society) worldviews, it's somewhat subtle, but looking in general - there it is.
So, if we are talking about Sel's inclination towards 'punishing' players for specific character traits behind the decisions they make, I think compliance may surely be one of those. Moreso considering philosophical depth and educative tendencies of the game. And even moreso, with Sel's trait in liking to have sadistic joy in toying with person's (character's) freedom of will deprivation, fun in illusion of free choice as in 'This Town Has Two Halves' or the one with Molly, somewhat his bruised ego's god's complex.
And I see the detail to prove it - you technically can't go red on Stomachache as it becomes 'different' event in such case.

I've made a couple posts about the event and why I went red path for it but as I read everyone's posts I started thinking more on it and it wasn't just a "moral" high ground that made me choose it, when the event happened and I chose the green path initially I felt pulled out of the story, not because I felt bad or grossed out (That came a bit after) but I remember watching the beginning of the event and the story losing me, it didn't make sense as a narrative to me, it felt out of place for where Sensei was in the story and his mindset at the time on top of how he had been interacting and treating Io. It has been the only time in this whole game where I paused because I felt a disconnect.

There are people who are calling it a master class and piece and what not but I don't agree, it felt...forced and disjointed, janky in a way. I've been green path this whole game, no matter the decision I went green cause every single time no matter the moral behind it, it felt like it fit, like a piece of the puzzle that is LiL, Stomachache didn't. So far I have not regretted my choice, MY choice, to do the red path of stomachache seeing the following events, we don't know where the story for her is going so for everyone rubbing their hands together salivating at the "punshiment" Sel will inflict on those who went red path with Io and making what looks like gymastic leaps of logic to discredit the red path (I have yet to feel or see any sort of anxienty or inevidable heel turn where he turns into a monster and breaks Io) You sound deluded to me.

I had a stray thought and what would be hilarious to me if Sel pulled a "Ha, Gotcha Bitch" and have one of her future events switch the path of Stomachache, turning the green path red and red path green in a statement of you are so focus chasing the 'right' path that you would do anything and everything to stay on it, cause chaos and carnage all around discord and forums for some convaluded reason or another. Maybe a statement on moral high ground and the player as a person, monsters and something something. Actually if that did happen (I know it's probably never gonna but) I would fly to these forums just to see the reaction and result.

posts.content_html_raw:
Mansy_mans said:
However, I do feel that the story progression is a bit slow at the beginning. I understand it's still early on, but I'm wondering if the story will become more engaging as it goes on and if there will be more dramatic moments. While I enjoy the character conversations, I’m hoping for some more dynamic and exciting events—nothing lewd, just moments that move the plot forward and bring more action to the story.
Click to expand...
If you're after 'action' it's not going to happen. It's a VN, not a FPS or some other game hidden in a VN. You will read, you will read a lot, and for all the words in probably the longest VN there is, you might get to make 30 choices or so (Not counting actual menuing to do your daily schedule / puzzle solving) There's also a lot of pretentious fluff surrounding events (intro and outtro text) that doesn't really go away, but the actual story within them is so worth working through that.

If you're after 'drama' you'll be well fed. Chapter 1 is slow compared to the rest of the game, because the game seems like a standard harem game to you. If you find the first happy event and aren't disgusted enough to reject the game like the other person did yesterday, you will eventually find the game can make you feel in such ways that you'd feel embarassed to admit to other people who aren't online. (like really, stopping the game and crying for a while because something bad happened to a fictional character??? are you 5?)

I'd highly recommend getting the guide mod before you make a choice that makes you miss events. If you don't like the grinding aspects of the game there is a autovn mod which seemed competent based on the one person I know who ran a complete playthrough using it. URM can let you see dialogue choices you're missing out on, and makes it easy to edit variables and other features that I don't use, but you need to show some restraint using it. Been several people breaking their saves because they can't stop clicking everything.

jclark1337 said:
Tbh I feel like you are having too much of a negative bias towards the outcomes of red path as a result of the story rarely allowing positive outcomes. You keep mentioning her fear, doubt, and frailty. I'm not denying that the possibility of a false hope is definitely there (and likely even) or that those characteristics aren't a core part of her personality deep down, but Io herself does not display these emotions any more than normal during the events following compared to green path. As a matter of fact, in red path she displays positivity and hope. This is the first time we've seen her in game take a single step toward the direction of "wait, maybe I'm not 100% trash... I might only be 90%" and actually seem...almost happy for once. Obviously this could very well end up turning on its head but from what we get in game red path doesn't directly allude to her being any more frail or scared. It's not something that we can see working out from what the story has given us thus far because barely anything really has before. But we know already that theoretically it eventually WILL happen with the purity routes.

That being said, it seems like that kind of meta-narrative shift is still a ways off. So the likelihood of an actual positive outcome like this is pretty low at this point, I do agree. However like I've said before, I just can't help but latch on to that idealized fantasy of giving her just a slice of hope and reassurance. I don't care if Selebus makes me regret it, I want so badly for this moment to be real for her. I will accept the consequences if it does end up backfiring and despair accordingly. The meaning of this story to me is to be able to face all of the struggles and tragedies this world has to offer and yet still continue to HOPE and see the beauty and light that exists in the vast sea of darkness.

I have to keep this reply brief but I have the time to highlight why Red vs. Green have a tendency to talk past each other, imo. It's heavily based on the readers relationship with anxiety and white lies.
Anxiety and fear of the unknown have been ever present, debilitating features of my life. I spent years having to convince myself I liked what I was doing or pushing aside doubts and shame and fears and restlessness in order to simply face the day. It comes with a nasty feature of my own voice nagging me about one worry or another all day, every day. It would often conclude that the answer was to stop entering the environment that caused the doubt, and slowly ramp up the mental torture until I did something to never go back to that place, no matter how much it shattered my life to do so.

Never, not even once, did those fears fade. The only thing that ever helped was knowing the full extent of what could happen and that I could handle what was in store. I became a person that fought to tell literally everyone as much truth as I possibly could, no matter how damaging it was to me. The act of lying to someone or lying to myself causes more anxiety and panic than almost any other thing I can do. I get one shot at it and if you ask "Really?" I cave instantly and find way to tell you the truth. Best I can do is say "I can't tell you, talk to X."

While not nearly as extreme, lemme tell you something else I share with Io. Well, moreso Akira than Io.

I was (static).

So yeah, my thoughts on Io path are practically 100% projection. I often throw myself in harm's way in pursuit of the truth, erego I respect that desire in her character. I find white lies and thin hope to be sickening and patronizing, erego when I think she's caught up in that I feel immense dread. I prefer to rip the bandaid so given a choice, I prefer the path that uses pain to avoid fear rather than the path that uses hope to avoid pain.

To me, hope is not salvation. It's a threat. For every hope I try to hold onto it creates twice as much fear.

For a brain like mine, hope is poison and truth is the only antidote. You are not wrong if you prefer red path, it just means you can trust in something fragile without it destroying you.

I'm not convinced Io could do the same.

posts.content_html_raw:
Mansy_mans said:
I'm wondering if the story will become more engaging as it goes on and if there will be more dramatic moments.
Click to expand...
Yes. The beginning of the game (first few updates, but, to an extent, the entire first chapter) is a slow burn, where Selebus gives you a "blank slate" protagonist whose goal is to fuck teenagers in a made up world without consequences. It's shallow on purpose.

As you advance, you discover more and more about the true nature of this "city" and about the protagonist. What seemed shallow was actually hinting at a lot of complexity. The replay value is off the charts. The dramatic moments come from what's being revealed being contrasted with what he's been doing, and what (and why) he can't help but do. Add in a few plot twists and the constant but paced revelations and that's where the dramatic moments will come from.

Do not play this game without the guide mod though. And everytime time you arrive at a "puzzle", use the puzzle guide as well.

I feel like you may be projecting. If that's the impression you got from the thread, let me reiterate for the friends I can safely represent on this matter that we couldn't care less. Obviously that doesn't account for everyone here, but surely for the larger (and saner) part.

Selebus is pretty adamant on "make of this game what you will", and it will not be some random group of people on a thread he doesn't even like that will try to tell you otherwise. Anyone can play however they want. More power to them.
That being said, "so for everyone rubbing their hands together salivating at the "punishment" Sel will inflict on those who went red path with Io and making what looks like gymnastic leaps of logic to discredit the red path [...] You sound deluded to me." - Respectfully, this is ignorance. The claims of punishment for the red path didn't come from an F95 echochamber, it came from the game itself:

Green path "purists", as you say, are less about inflicting pain on the red path players, and much more about seeing their suffering being justified by Akira growing and being able to fulfill what Himawari said so long ago:

Moonflare said:
I feel like you may be projecting. If that's the impression you got from the thread, let me reiterate for the friends I can safely represent on this matter that we couldn't care less. Obviously that doesn't account for everyone here, but surely for the larger (and saner) part.

Selebus is pretty adamant on "make of this game what you will", and it will not be some random group of people on a thread he doesn't even like that will try to tell you otherwise. Anyone can play however they want. More power to them.
That being said, "so for everyone rubbing their hands together salivating at the "punishment" Sel will inflict on those who went red path with Io and making what looks like gymnastic leaps of logic to discredit the red path [...] You sound deluded to me." - Respectfully, this is ignorance. The claims of punishment for the red path didn't come from an F95 echochamber, it came from the game itself:
View attachment 4719440 View attachment 4719441 View attachment 4719443
The text is pretty clear, by choosing to confront the terrible things of the green path, Akira is growing. If he doesn't, he remains weak. Soon enough, he won't be able to catch up. This is straight from the game.

Green path "purists", as you say, are less about inflicting pain on the red path players, and much more about seeing their suffering being justified by Akira growing and being able to fulfill what Himawari said so long ago:
View attachment 4719468 View attachment 4719469
Basically, that there is purpose to all of this. And even if there is no punishment whatsoever, that was never the point.

The point was that the greater the trials Akira and the girls have to go through, the more believable and rewarding will be their endings - both in a narrative sense and in a practical one, since Selebus just hasn't written a better story by missing events that he wanted to put in his story in the first place. For instance, the Yumi situation if "Matador" is missed barely makes sense.
It is unfortunate that so many people felt attacked as if we were telling that they were wrong in playing however they want. That was not our intention. Hopefully, we can move on from this with the mutual understanding that saying that the green path is the truer story doesn't equate to saying that one is wrong by choosing to miss events.
Click to expand...
After going through the thread again I have to admit, with it having been 5:30am in the morning and I had been recovering from being sick there was a bit of confusion but the ones I was talking about who were mentioning punishments for red path were Bingoogus (Though his was a lighter, lesser extent) and LessonsInDissonance who was far more harsh in their posts and may of annoyed me (And with it being so late and me being mildly out of it, it felt like more people then it was)
So less projecting and more not narrowing my focus on my response as it felt more like LessonsInDissonance being the one rubbing their hands etc. Also I feel a miffed being called ignorant but I'll let it slide to respond what you've shown feels like you're talking about isn't punishment, it's consequence. To me they are different in that a punishment is inflicted by another to you as a response to your actions (IE you stole money and get arrested and put in jail) While a consequence is a result of your actions across everyone (IE you stole money, now who ever you stole that money from can't buy what they need, your choice to steal money means someone has less of it, because you stole money you can then be arrested and put in jail for breaking a law)

With that being said some of the not so sane (In your words) Green Path purists have implied (Even in previous discussions of Stomachache) that Sel will go out of his way to punish those like myself who went red path by doing something horrible to Io that will be worst then stomachache and simply break Io instead of writing a flowing narrative which shows the consequences of choosing the red path which doesn't make sense to me as the narrative he is writing.

Now like I said earlier I have also gone green path all the way, every green path choice I had the option to do, I did cause to me it fit, it made sense to the story, but Stomachache didn't (Even when I went back and replayed it) for some reason my brain just disconnected from the story when it happened, like it was a piece of the story shaped like a triangle being put into a circle hole. It's the only red choice I made and it was simply cause I can't not see the green path as an organic part of the story and feel natural to where it was. If it was by it self with none of the story before it or a scene in the general story of LiL then yes I can see it making sense to the overall story but where and when it happened, I can not connect it. it just doesn't make sense and I think until those consequences happen it won't to me.

You don't have to make a response to me if you feel no need to as this is now just me replying and rambling what I think and don't think anything said will change that, if you do want to respond then please I do enjoy reading your thoughts along with many others in this forum but I'm not sure if I will respond after this or not.

After going through the thread again I have to admit, with it having been 5:30am in the morning and I had been recovering from being sick there was a bit of confusion but the ones I was talking about who were mentioning punishments for red path were Bingoogus (Though his was a lighter, lesser extent) and LessonsInDissonance who was far more harsh in their posts and may of annoyed me (And with it being so late and me being mildly out of it, it felt like more people then it was)
So less projecting and more not narrowing my focus on my response as it felt more like LessonsInDissonance being the one rubbing their hands etc. Also I feel a miffed being called ignorant but I'll let it slide to respond what you've shown feels like you're talking about isn't punishment, it's consequence. To me they are different in that a punishment is inflicted by another to you as a response to your actions (IE you stole money and get arrested and put in jail) While a consequence is a result of your actions across everyone (IE you stole money, now who ever you stole that money from can't buy what they need, your choice to steal money means someone has less of it, because you stole money you can then be arrested and put in jail for breaking a law)

With that being said some of the not so sane (In your words) Green Path purists have implied (Even in previous discussions of Stomachache) that Sel will go out of his way to punish those like myself who went red path by doing something horrible to Io that will be worst then stomachache and simply break Io instead of writing a flowing narrative which shows the consequences of choosing the red path which doesn't make sense to me as the narrative he is writing.

Now like I said earlier I have also gone green path all the way, every green path choice I had the option to do, I did cause to me it fit, it made sense to the story, but Stomachache didn't (Even when I went back and replayed it) for some reason my brain just disconnected from the story when it happened, like it was a piece of the story shaped like a triangle being put into a circle hole. It's the only red choice I made and it was simply cause I can't not see the green path as an organic part of the story and feel natural to where it was. If it was by it self with none of the story before it or a scene in the general story of LiL then yes I can see it making sense to the overall story but where and when it happened, I can not connect it. it just doesn't make sense and I think until those consequences happen it won't to me.

You don't have to make a response to me if you feel no need to as this is now just me replying and rambling what I think and don't think anything said will change that, if you do want to respond then please I do enjoy reading your thoughts along with many others in this forum but I'm not sure if I will respond after this or not.

posts.content_html_raw:
I wouldn't judge anyone of either group.
I think the decision in Stomachache is a very individual one.

I'm a completionist and also like to theorize, so i had to go with the green path because it's very likely that the green path contains the most lore info. In a perfect world i would have chosen the other option though.

That being said, there's one thing that i don't completely get.
And that's how some people pretend to shrug things like that off and say "Thats just pixels, how can you xyz...", and at the same time post something like their fav char tier lists.
With Sel being the most hypocritical, in a way, of all, with him saying the exact same about wizard contend.
Does he want us to be invested in the story and characters or not?

In the end it's about one's own individual decisions and individual moral concept i think, unless one managed to be completely detached of it all ofc.
I also don't think there's anything bad in warning people about the technicalities, that one might miss "plot" in the red path, in an informative way.

I understand that not everyone has the same attachment to this game, but I feel like if you willingly choose to not do the green route, you are one of many things.
It is in my interest that these characters get their happy ending whether they are real or not, and this is something that you can only do if you're playing the green route.

I agree with Selebus' stance on making near impossible reset puzzles, it assures that only those who are truly invested in the game, will go out of their way to bypass these checkpoints. What I don't agree with is the draconian measures and punishments delivered to people that want to seek help. 99% of you here watched a guide and so what? you are not any less in love with the game than those that haven't cheated.

My bepuzzlement comes from the fact that after so many years, there's people that would willingly not do green path. It comes from a place where I assume that you are fully aware of how things work in this game, after so many years it would be impossible at this point not to understand that you are sentencing all the people in this game to their doom if you don't follow the green path, and you're doing this because you're either weak, ignorant or heartless.
Because you were weak, you couldn't bring yourself to do stomachache, or you were ignorant not to know that it would be best to see it in the long run, or, you are fully aware of what will happen and still sentence this world to collapse regardless.

It's not your fault if you can't remember every detail or forget things, it's not your fault if you don't know how to do something, it's not your fault if you're not perfect. It is however, a fault in you if you can't be bothered to try.

And here we see the zealotry of the netizen in its native habitat. Surrounded by the familiar haze of their computer screen, the netizen looks for wrongdoers infiltrating their digital territory and flares it's languid crest to mark it's claim. The netizen has no legitimate claim to this territory, but they cannot resist the urge to protect whatever dark corner of the digital world they nest in.

Possession of another's experience? None of us have that right.

People talked about it why and i agree all of it. While some people warmed up to her because of recent events i still dislike her. To be fair, i dislike the way Selebus use her. Moonflare said:
It's my random musings about chapter 2 again. So, this isn't about a single event, but more about the general outline of certain plotlines upon rewatch. And a few random tidbits at the end:

1. Firstly, about the Otoha x Rin thing. I find it interesting that, regardless of how things will go, their relationship seemed doomed from the start by things I didn't really recall.
When they first start their relationship, Otoha was afraid that she was going to be Rin's rebound after Chika. And later it's revealed through a game of truth and dare that Chika would have dated Rin if Akira didn't show up.

View attachment 4390576

Now, obviously, this doesn't make Otoha's fears true. Rin was not using her as a rebound, she truly jumped into the relationship. The issue is that Rin is very hormonal, and although I believe she was being truthful in everything, the sad truth is that she loved Akira - while her feelings for Otoha were much more hormonal than having someone that actually cared for her in a healthy way (yeah, that one was Akira, shocking, right?).

View attachment 4390584

And I'm not talking just about him being her father figure, although that's obviously true. I mean love love, especially on the good homie path.

View attachment 4390585

After getting together with Otoha she still has her depression/cutting episodes because, yeah, that's how actual clinical depression works. And after her recovery she confesses that she loves him. Multiple times in fact. It's just not something that she's ready to face in a romantic manner (especially when she already has a girlfriend and Futaba - and all the others, like Chika - love him as well, and are more advanced in it than she is), but it is there.

View attachment 4390589

This leads Rin to trying to set him up with others in bizarre ways, like compelling him to actually date Futaba, making her very uncomfortable. She does the same to other people as well, albeit not that strongly. I think this happens because she wants him to be in a relationship so that she can settle her love for him in a safer way.

View attachment 4390592

Regarding Otoha part of the deal, she has to ditch Rin during the christmas party because of her parents and reveals that they don't know about her. This leads to Akira trying to help her reconcile with Rin, which leads to him seeing her being attracted to Niki during lessons - which Niki says that she's aware of and it is to be expected of everyone anyway, and they're teenagers. I don't have enough evidence at the moment to ascertain if Rin was supposed to be a "rebound" for Niki at this point, but it does seem like Otoha likes Rin at the very least.

View attachment 4390597

I feel like it's ironic that they're on this double date because Rin loves Akira, and Otoha is attracted to Niki. Although obviously Rin is being taken advantage of by Otoha, because, again, Rin puts herself in this position by putting her all onto someone that barely gives anything back (something that Otoha would point out in the future).

Basically, they're teenagers doing teenage stuff. All this rambling is just because this happened:

View attachment 4390605 View attachment 4390606

And yes, that is basically what breaks them in the end. This is not a perfect prediction of course because it's not that Otoha eventually breaks up with Rin because of her being a girl, but rather because she's another girl. Rin will keep making herself a victim of their relationship, and Otoha will keep taking advantage of her until enough is enough.

Funnily enough, from Akira's perspective, he muses that it is this relationship blowing up in Rin's face that would ultimately lead her to him 100%, and that Otoha being attracted to Niki would lead her in his direction as well. So for him everything is a-okay - with the exception of Rin being hurt. But I'm talking from memory about these future events, so I'm looking forward to them in the replay.
2. Multiple Maya smiles to remind everyone that I had to drink a lot of water after this event (This isn't a joke, I cried so much that I had to stop playing for some time).
View attachment 4390623 View attachment 4390622 View attachment 4390625 View attachment 4390624 View attachment 4390626 View attachment 4390627 View attachment 4390628 View attachment 4390629
View attachment 4390637

She just loves him so much.
3. And lastly, it's heartwarming to see Yumi caring about Akira.
View attachment 4390642

There was this scene where he delivers her Yuki's gift, and for a moment she thinks it's his. And man... The only reason that she's not his girlfriend is because Akira doesn't want it. Because if he dropped the other girls and actually made an effort for two or three events, she'd be his.

View attachment 4390650

Then when she meets Yuki again, Akira is extremely respectful to Yumi - which leads to her testing him in a moment of vulnerability to see if he'd kiss her again:

View attachment 4390651

Akira blacks out in the middle of this and fights hard to not do anything, and manages to say he won't hurt her. And she's visibly torn between wanting him to kiss her and being happy that she can trust him a bit more.

View attachment 4390655

Then, when she apologises to Futaba and stops her bullying entirely, he says he's proud of her. And despite what she says, she's clearly thankful for his support.

View attachment 4390657
4. Oh, I also have these:
Yasu waited until everyone was gone to try the karaoke because she didn't want to bother anyone.

View attachment 4390662

she gets embarrassed that Akira heard her, but then turns happy when he compliments her and says that she'll try hard to become better.

View attachment 4390663

Noriko is really pitiful because everytime she gets with Akira she either breaks down crying or puts many restrictions on them becoming intimate, which only makes it so that Akira gets back together with Niki before her (and a lot of people too). i understand why she does this of course, but it's still pitiful due to how much it backfires.

View attachment 4390667
View attachment 4390671

Chika first shows her "I get it" tendencies around this time as well. As she tries to play boyfriend/girlfriend in school and at the mall, and Akira tells her that she really needs to slowdown. Like, she actually asks him for her and Chinami to move in and get Ami out of the house in three years (???). Well, from this moment on she kind of made herself a prisoner of her feelings and we know where that led.

View attachment 4390674

Molly's deal wasn't as hard to deal with it in retrospect. And the problem really was just Akira being, in the words of our one true bro, a little bitch. Now, I'm not condoning his actions, but the truth of the matter is that Molly had already masturbated, changed clothes and even talked about experimenting with him. IF Akira was the actual scumbag he is sometimes, he'd have lied about it. "yeah, you were drunk and I guess I should have rejected you, but we ended up playing around and that was it". Problem solved.

All he did was not do anything, and Molly had to reach this conclusion, apologise to him and then when he said he didn't remember, she had them agree on the best possible possibility about what had happened. So yeah, huge nothingburger. Although I guess it allowed Kirin to declare that she'd be okay with him raping people if she could watch.

View attachment 4390684

Himawari's first appearance, that Akira will remember, also happens around this time, after he leaves Sara's appartment and finds himself outside the school that Maya takes him to. I mention this because Maya also says that the festival takes place in a district where buses don't go anymore, on account of the school over there having been deactivated.

So it's likely to be this school (and also Sara's school, that he visits during a happy event - and also possibly Sekai's school, and further possibly the school that we see during that one happy event where Akira is talking to Maya at the roof and she's his girlfriend), which also is in the same district with the out of order shrine that we see during Maya's date (likely). Just thought I'd mention it.

spoilers.title: assortment of random stuff
spoilers.html:
Yasu waited until everyone was gone to try the karaoke because she didn't want to bother anyone.

View attachment 4390662

she gets embarrassed that Akira heard her, but then turns happy when he compliments her and says that she'll try hard to become better.

View attachment 4390663

Noriko is really pitiful because everytime she gets with Akira she either breaks down crying or puts many restrictions on them becoming intimate, which only makes it so that Akira gets back together with Niki before her (and a lot of people too). i understand why she does this of course, but it's still pitiful due to how much it backfires.

View attachment 4390667
View attachment 4390671

Chika first shows her "I get it" tendencies around this time as well. As she tries to play boyfriend/girlfriend in school and at the mall, and Akira tells her that she really needs to slowdown. Like, she actually asks him for her and Chinami to move in and get Ami out of the house in three years (???). Well, from this moment on she kind of made herself a prisoner of her feelings and we know where that led.

View attachment 4390674

Molly's deal wasn't as hard to deal with it in retrospect. And the problem really was just Akira being, in the words of our one true bro, a little bitch. Now, I'm not condoning his actions, but the truth of the matter is that Molly had already masturbated, changed clothes and even talked about experimenting with him. IF Akira was the actual scumbag he is sometimes, he'd have lied about it. "yeah, you were drunk and I guess I should have rejected you, but we ended up playing around and that was it". Problem solved.

All he did was not do anything, and Molly had to reach this conclusion, apologise to him and then when he said he didn't remember, she had them agree on the best possible possibility about what had happened. So yeah, huge nothingburger. Although I guess it allowed Kirin to declare that she'd be okay with him raping people if she could watch.

View attachment 4390684

Himawari's first appearance, that Akira will remember, also happens around this time, after he leaves Sara's appartment and finds himself outside the school that Maya takes him to. I mention this because Maya also says that the festival takes place in a district where buses don't go anymore, on account of the school over there having been deactivated.

So it's likely to be this school (and also Sara's school, that he visits during a happy event - and also possibly Sekai's school, and further possibly the school that we see during that one happy event where Akira is talking to Maya at the roof and she's his girlfriend), which also is in the same district with the out of order shrine that we see during Maya's date (likely). Just thought I'd mention it.

Click to expand...
No, when you permanently miss an event the text will be red with a line struck through it. The event title will also change. If it's still in black like that it just means you've not done the event yet. If I remember rightly this is one of Rin's early events, you just need to go see her in the cafe on a weekend with like 5 affection.

It's important to remember not to focus too much on one character in this game - remember, this is a lengthy VN, not a generic porn game. Don't focus on your favourite girl, try to balance your time between all the girls and raise their affection fairly evenly or you'll really slow yourself down - a lot of the main story events require you to have done specific character events.

If you're not already it's highly recommended you use the walkthrough mod, or else look up the next main quest on the wiki and check the requirements if you find yourself stuck for a while. It's not a big deal at the stage of the game you're in at the moment but before too long you'll be juggling 35 characters with main story events requiring a specific event from just one or two of them and other events having one-off hard to guess triggers
