posts.content_html_raw:
When Chinami was very young she was able to get medical care thanks to an unnamed friend of Chiaki who pretended to be her mom. A while back, I speculated that the friend could have been Tsubasa. Thanks to new evidence, I now believe that theory is extremely likely to be true. Here's the original post:
aramaug said:
I'm glad someone brought this up. She might be referring to Sekai, but I think it's actually Chiaki. Here's the line:
View attachment 3993628
I can't remember if it's been established that Chiaki had a temper, but I imagine Chika is emulating her when she curses in Tagalog.
View attachment 3993633
In "Curry Night" Chiaki talks about having a friend take Chinami to the hospital.
View attachment 3993654 View attachment 3993655 View attachment 3993658 View attachment 3993659 View attachment 3993660
The friend is strangely intimidating and has connections; sure sounds like Tsubasa to me.
View attachment 3993694 View attachment 3993695 View attachment 3993696
I also think this makes a lot of sense with Tsubasa's actions. The meeting at the hot spring always felt engineered, and she was remarkably quick to latch onto the Chosokabes as her "new daughters". My guess is she's been keeping tabs on them since Chiaki died and finally decided to get directly involved in their lives.

As for how they could have met, Tsubasa used to "sneak away" from her rich girl lifestyle in her youth:
View attachment 3993756 View attachment 3993757
Click to expand...
In Yasu's first event in 0.48, Touka uses intimidation and her family's connections to force a doctor to give Yasu treatment as if she were a member of Touka's family. This is very similar to what Chiaki's friend did for Chinami, and enough details are repeated that I can't see it being a coincidence. Rather, the parallels are because the person who taught Touka to act like this, i.e. Tsubasa, is the same person as Chiaki's friend.
The hospital that Touka takes Yasu to is dependent on Tsukioka family donations. Chiaki's friend is able to get Chinami care because of her connections at a hospital.

Yasu is using the Tsukioka's connections and "benefits". Chinami used her benefactor's connections and insurance.
Touka gets what she wants by threatening the doctor, causing Yasu to remark how scary she seems. Chiaki's friend was capable of being intimidating to get things done.
Furthermore, Touka explicitly says that she learned her strategy of intimidation from Tsubasa herself.
Tsubasa also taught her you can make people like you by giving them money - exactly what Tsubasa did with the hospital.
If Tsubasa was Chiaki's friend, it raises an obvious question: why didn't she use her vast wealth to do more for the Chosokabes? For example, she could have paid for Chinami's care outright instead of only letting them use her insurance. I think Tsubasa herself gave us an explanation for why she didn't do more: Chiaki stubbornly refused direct financial assistance.
Shortly after Tsubasa hears the story about how Chiaki got help from her friend, she says that if Chika doesn't accept Tsubasa's aid, she's going to wind up like Chiaki. Based on what Tsubasa should know, this comparison makes little sense - Chiaki accepted aid but still died in poverty. On the other hand, it makes a lot of sense if she has personal knowledge that Chiaki rejected offers of more substantial help.

So it seems like Chiaki let her friend commit insurance fraud but wouldn't let her use her own money to pay legally, which is a bit silly, but I guess she drew a hard line on accepting money and that was the only other way she could afford Chinami's care.

Shortly after Tsubasa hears the story about how Chiaki got help from her friend, she says that if Chika doesn't accept Tsubasa's aid, she's going to wind up like Chiaki. Based on what Tsubasa should know, this comparison makes little sense - Chiaki accepted aid but still died in poverty. On the other hand, it makes a lot of sense if she has personal knowledge that Chiaki rejected offers of more substantial help.
So it seems like Chiaki let her friend commit insurance fraud but wouldn't let her use her own money to pay legally, which is a bit silly, but I guess she drew a hard line on accepting money and that was the only other way she could afford Chinami's care.

Tsubasa also taught her you can make people like you by giving them money - exactly what Tsubasa did with the hospital.

posts.content_html_raw:
Call me overly optimistic, but I feel like this Dorm Wars will end up being pretty fun. Sure, there probably won't be any huge strides lore-wise, but the interactions themselves can still be interesting.

Take the Date War contest with Rin VS Io for example. We're coming off an insane setup in Rin's story. She was actually gonna go through with having sex with Akira after so long of holding back, but was unlucky enough for her mom to find out. Akira and Rin haven't spoken to one another since before that incident even took place, so now we get to see where that leads. Let's not forget Haruka also told Akira about it, so that makes things extra interesting.

And with Io, maybe she'll finally get that long awaited amusement park date she's always wanted. Sure, she went with Uta recently, but it was cut short and she didn't get to experience it fully. This could be the perfect opportunity for it to happen.

And that's just the contest I look forward to the most. I'm also curious what this lawyer competition will wind up being... All I know is Makoto and Uta look amazing in those suits, hot dayum.

On another note, I find it amusing that Yumi is actively participating in her contest with seemingly no resistance at all. It's almost like she wants to show off for Akira in her swimsuit or something, but just won't admit it.

I see you, Yumi... We all know how your last event ended...

Last Dorm Wars (0.39) kicked rocks due to its chaotic and random nature, the constant barrage of Good Kid songs distracting many players from reading, and the fact that Akira wasn't even directly part of the event itself. That was the peak of his depression arc and, while necessary in the long term, it only made the update a slog to get through rather than an enjoyable experience.

With all that said, though, I'm willing to give this Dorm Wars a chance at redemption.

There were rumors circulating that the contests for this upcoming Dorm Wars were decided by the LiLcord via polls, but I can confirm that's 100% not true. There was a channel for Dorm Wars ideas during the Fanfest where members could toss ideas around, but it never reached the point where actual polls were made for voting on each individual contest. The update's writing is all on Sel like normal.

The above screnshot made wonder.

Does maya have an issue with getting touched? We know she was abused by a family member, so it's normal that she has a problem with touching for a normal teenage girl. And Maya is totally normal teenage girl. Especially this one, because new Maya didn't live for a thousand years.

Which made me question another thing.

Maya still can't remember her parents or where she come form. According to Ami she just showed up and they became best friends. Can't share screenshots right now but on second beach event in chapter 3 Ami says this:

"What if we threw away all of our secrets and just moved forward together? Like the way things were when you first showed up?"
Then she says this:
We attached so quickly... It was almost like we knew each other already or something.

It made me question the timelines.

I thought when everything completely resets, it goes back to start of the loops. Waking up in classroom, introduced to the world by Ami. Original class of 10 etc. In this timeline Akira made a career of a teacher, and Maya and Ami already knows each other. All the reset talk with Maya made me believe this. We go back to classroom everytime hard reset happens.

But the way Ami talk about Maya makes me think, the loops started way before then. Thats how she knew Ami so good, and became friends quickly.

Then another question comes up, if beginning of the loops is way before than og game start, why Akira getting reset make the world revert the world to the og game start?

This made me think about terminals.

If you made sense of my ramblings above, i am trying to say starting point of loops change, a change happens towards further in time. Like this:


Point A (resets reverts to this)----->Point B (Resets revert to this) Maya and Ami become friends------>Point C current loops.

We know Akira is important and him getting reset would mean a hard reset. Everything would revert to point C and sensei starts with a new personality. So it would be logical to think point A and B had other important characters that loops revolve around right?

It would not be wrong to assume that Point A or B character was Yuu from terminal 22. Loops were all around him. Then something happened and it change the person and the terminal. And loops are focused on a different person on a different time and a different terminal.

By the time between Yuu and Akira, there was a point of loops in which Ami and Maya became friends. So between Yuu and Akira there was another person that loops focused on. And that person is probably Sekai.


And now, one of the biggest question i had while playing the game:

You may ask: "But fasoaga, if Yuu was in terminal 22 and Akira in in terminal 23 how it was possible that Sekai was between them"

I think the reason why "am i okay" calls us Sekai and why Akira cast shadow of Sekai in memories is Terminal 23 is not for Akira but Sekai.

I made a previous post about Futaba's horror story and Sekai. I ramble about it much more in there.
Shortly, in"chapter 3 Cicadas Rhythm" Futaba tells a horror story about a girl who accidently wandered to a town frozen in time. In this town nobody can make a sound, similar to Nao-chan. In this town, the girl wanders to a tall building and climbs it. Towards the end girl loses her ability to make a sound. Then she gets pushed down the stairs by a cat.

Since the game continuously makes connection with cats and Maya, i made a theory that Sekai was the original loops character. But for some reason, Maya gave away her powers or knowledge to get rid of Sekai without destroying the terminal. This way Sekai got replaced by Akira and reverting point of loops changed. Akira is just a false title holder of Sekai.


What this theory explains:
-Why am i okay calls Akira, Sekai.
-Why Maya can't remember the loops, after getting reset to a point AFTER she can use the power of loops to befriend Ami.
-Connection between paradolia and Sekai? Because Paradolia is not the voice inside the head of Akira, it is the voice inside the head of SEKAI.
-Repeating theme of "LET ME OUT"

What this theory doesn't explain:

Please fill this place.

Gods of the lore please read this and give your opinion. I just wanted to point something about Maya and it got out of my hands. Sorry for any grammer mistakes.

It would not be wrong to assume that Point A or B character was Yuu from terminal 22. Loops were all around him. Then something happened and it change the person and the terminal. And loops are focused on a different person on a different time and a different terminal.
By the time between Yuu and Akira, there was a point of loops in which Ami and Maya became friends. So between Yuu and Akira there was another person that loops focused on. And that person is probably Sekai.

spoilers.title: Why "Am I Okay" calls him that name?
spoilers.html:
You may ask: "But fasoaga, if Yuu was in terminal 22 and Akira in in terminal 23 how it was possible that Sekai was between them"

I think the reason why "am i okay" calls us Sekai and why Akira cast shadow of Sekai in memories is Terminal 23 is not for Akira but Sekai.

I made a previous post about Futaba's horror story and Sekai. I ramble about it much more in there.
Shortly, in"chapter 3 Cicadas Rhythm" Futaba tells a horror story about a girl who accidently wandered to a town frozen in time. In this town nobody can make a sound, similar to Nao-chan. In this town, the girl wanders to a tall building and climbs it. Towards the end girl loses her ability to make a sound. Then she gets pushed down the stairs by a cat.

Since the game continuously makes connection with cats and Maya, i made a theory that Sekai was the original loops character. But for some reason, Maya gave away her powers or knowledge to get rid of Sekai without destroying the terminal. This way Sekai got replaced by Akira and reverting point of loops changed. Akira is just a false title holder of Sekai.

-Repeating theme of "LET ME OUT"

Moonflare said:
3. Who's this world made by and who got left behind. There are a ton of possibilities. Amy's boyfriend left her at the mall with her mom. Ami has mentioned on their bus ride backwards ("Somnambula") that when they are alone at the end of the world it would be nice if Akira could ride them around, suggesting Ami (or the entity inside her aka super Ami) has been left by Akira multiple times at the end of a cycle. In "Perfect Harmony", the narrator states that their perfect gate could never be reached in their world because Akira (assumed) left it. Which is referenced again by Nodoka at "Perfect hair forever", telling him they met because he left sooner than he was supposed to.

As for who the world is for, we just got confirmation that 22 is likely Yuu's world and 23 is Akira's. Unless Selebus wishes to bring in the concept of a world made for the interloper/player that takes agency on that world by inserting itself into Yuu or Akira, then it's likely made for them (as they're in the center of it).

That however begs the question what their objective is, since, if it's to prepare a vessel to ride around in, then from Kyoto we get the feeling that Kaori/Sekai was that objective achieving fruition, and yet, there is no terminal 22.5 that is for Sekai/Kaori.

Another possible solution is that 23 was never Akira's to begin with, but Sekai's world. Akira doesn't reside in apartment 23, it's Kaori/Sekaori that do. It would certainly explain why the gods, although interested in him, don't seem to place him at the center of their plans. Mind you, we could also interpret Pareidolia saying that he waited such a long time to board Kaori as "boarding Kaori is what allows him to make spring arrive".

In that sense, HOPE, Wires, Pareidolia and USER4 control the seasons from inside Kaori, which makes Kaori the real center of 23 (or rather, True Sekai).

I'll be taking another look at First Contact, but it might be the case that the appearance of the four from the wall that was broken with Sekai's death is actually their first boarding of Kaori/Sekai. The person that is "still behind the wheel" would be Sekai. This story was really never about Akira, it was about her.
Click to expand...
That being said, I think it's all very interesting. Ami holds a lot of answers, although it isn't clear that she has full access to them herself at all times. We got confirmation that Akira's home is 22, and there have been some references to 24 being either wrong, or about to come through.

More to your point, I think there's enough to assume that Sekai plays a center role (or was supposed to play that role before her untimely death, thus condemning Kaori to it by association). From what we've seen and assumed, she was being groomed to it. There is not enough however to conclude that Akira isn't the central character, because he could simply be influenced by either a willing or unwilling Sekai, which would be enough to call him Sekai (either because he's playing her role, or has traces of her), and yet still retain his protagonism.

This next post is all about Akira being Sekai in multiple interpretations of what that could be like:
Moonflare said:
1. Akira is Sekai in a traumatic sense.
2. Akira is with Sekai in a paranormal sense.
3. Akira is with Sekai in a psychological sense.

We have seen Sekai with Akira a number of times. Both as his shadow (in the early game), as in his flashback triggered from Niki's letters, possibly in Yasu's monologue to him in "Frankincense" (about the one that follows him, although that may not be Sekai), but, most important of all, through many dialogues that state that Sekai is bound to him as a lifeline to not disappear.
Sekai is his shadow.
View attachment 4678007
Thus, in that sense, he sort of is Sekai. It is also possible that he actually is Sekai in a more Sekaori kind of way. One option for that would be that he's playing out Sekai's original role. Thus, Akira is the player occupying the position that should have been Sekai's in 23. That would explain why Am I Okay addresses him as such, especially at a time when "Akira" wasn't as aware of who he was.

A number of recent events hint at that possibility. Akira's home is not 23, but 22. Both Sekai and Akira are children of Yuu (the previous protagonist), and thus capable of carrying his "legacy/curse". We infer that Sekai had been prepared to serve as a hotel for gods, which, ultimately, ended up with Kaori being cursed with that job since she took in what remained of Sekai. This puts both of them in a similar situation in relation to the gods and the overall grand scheme of things.

Finally, this relationship has been revisited both in Maki's last event (where Sekai seems to be a figment of Akira's imagination) - and, at the same time, a possible unwilling participant in his infection by her "bad" parts (the real Sekai that is) - as seen in Karin's event "Uzbekistan".
View attachment 4678008
View attachment 4674529
It seems like a worm was implanted into Sekai and it's not helping her in her objective. She's then desperate to not let the worm reach Akira, but seems to fail to do so.
Edit: Aramaug has pointed out that the last conversation could be Sekai talking about Ami as well.

All in all, good questions and theories.

By the time between Yuu and Akira, there was a point of loops in which Ami and Maya became friends. So between Yuu and Akira there was another person that loops focused on. And that person is probably Sekai.

spoilers.title: Why "Am I Okay" calls him that name?
spoilers.html:
You may ask: "But fasoaga, if Yuu was in terminal 22 and Akira in in terminal 23 how it was possible that Sekai was between them"

I think the reason why "am i okay" calls us Sekai and why Akira cast shadow of Sekai in memories is Terminal 23 is not for Akira but Sekai.

I made a previous post about Futaba's horror story and Sekai. I ramble about it much more in there.
Shortly, in"chapter 3 Cicadas Rhythm" Futaba tells a horror story about a girl who accidently wandered to a town frozen in time. In this town nobody can make a sound, similar to Nao-chan. In this town, the girl wanders to a tall building and climbs it. Towards the end girl loses her ability to make a sound. Then she gets pushed down the stairs by a cat.

Since the game continuously makes connection with cats and Maya, i made a theory that Sekai was the original loops character. But for some reason, Maya gave away her powers or knowledge to get rid of Sekai without destroying the terminal. This way Sekai got replaced by Akira and reverting point of loops changed. Akira is just a false title holder of Sekai.


What this theory explains:
-Why am i okay calls Akira, Sekai.
-Why Maya can't remember the loops, after getting reset to a point AFTER she can use the power of loops to befriend Ami.
-Connection between paradolia and Sekai? Because Paradolia is not the voice inside the head of Akira, it is the voice inside the head of SEKAI.

What this theory doesn't explain:

Please fill this place.

One of the minor things DeSkel has brought to surface is one of the greatest contributions, imo, that have been delivered by the recent FanFest, which is the wishing dimension of the resets.
Maya had to concentrate to "do" the resetting, she closed her eyes, and it was almost like she was praying. She also mentioned she had to concentrate to get it right, even though she didn't have full control of everything. She was also praying to a god she either didn't believe in, or hated. If you put all of this together with the "wishing dimension" of things, it makes perfect sense.

She had to concentrate to get her "wish" right (which explains the scope of it, the more detailed the wish the more effort she had to put into it), you also don't really have to have a strong relationship with a god to wish for something, you just do it (believing or not that someone is listening). It would also explain why anyone can do it, even BigBoi - it's literally just wishing for it when the world is at its end.

The Apocalypse Squad of the Forever Young spinoff makes mention of rotating between them in order to make their own wishes to reset each time. And even though all of this is a silly spinoff, I'd wager that the wishing thing is for real. It just fits way too well (including the recent voice urging Yumi to make a wish, and the aspect of the wishing being the thing that throws one into the wishing well - aka as another reality where their wish comes true).

All of which is to say that whilst the girls might not be "hard reset" the same way Maya's been I do think that when a Sensei dies/gets wiped and is replaced the world/timeline is and the girls are reformatted more extensively as a result.

thebadpastor said:
I agree with the point that the girls behaviour towards him is influenced by their unremembered past experiences with him but on a conscious level at the start of the game they all (excluding Ami, Ayane and Maya) treat Sensei as if he's a relatively new teacher with whom they have no personal relationship. This isn't the case throughout the game with subsequent resets, they have years worth of memories with him going back to the start of the game and treat him accordingly and simply aren't able to even try to address why that doesn't add up.

Likewise we know that prior Sensei's had things things like Dorm Wars and Halloween parties but these events are originally treated like something new by all the girls, not a recurring event, and these seem to be pretty identical to what we experienced in the game previously (same Halloween costumes, same Dorm Wars event). Maya Prime also both laments and enjoys the fact that once they get past the third reset everything's new to her, implying that what she's been experiencing all this time is mostly the same events over and over again (outside of a few temporary anomalies like a class transfer).

All of which is to say that whilst the girls might not be "hard reset" the same way Maya's been I do think that when a Sensei dies/gets wiped and is replaced the world/timeline is and the girls are reformatted more extensively as a result.
Click to expand...
Memories are virtually reset for the girls who aren't aware of things, but their subconscious feelings still seem to carry over to a degree.

This doesn't just apply to the love squad. Hence stuff like this since Chapter 1:
Rin - "What's it like, Sensei?"
- "Gaining the affection of others without ever really doing anything to earn it?"
- "Not insulting you. Just an observation."
- "You're very important to me as well but, in some way or another, I feel like you've always been important to me."

- "I had a crazy dream the other night, Sensei. Do you want to hear about it."
- "It was a dream of a new world."
- "It was the same world as this one. But it was one where we got to redo all of our mistakes."
- "Kind of like a reset button."
(Chapter 1 Rin 'Nothing Was Different' Event)

All of the girls likely feel things from their past, even after being reset, whether they are aware of it or not. This seems to be what Maya Prime was meaning by her reformatting example:
Maya Prime - "Didn't you think it was strange how quickly some of them warmed up to you despite undergoing a complete switch in personalities?"
- "How everyone just decided that not actually being taught anymore was a totally normal thing?"
- "What you were experiencing in watching those girls adapt to you was a type of reformatting."
(Chapter 2 Maya 'Now More Than Ever' Event)

New things are new to the girls, but they also seem to feel natural or expected to them, like they've done it before. It's likely the main reason that the girls are so familiar and lenient with Sensei from the start.

Their memories also seem to become more like dreams that only a few acknowledge. Makoto, Rin, Sensei, Tsuneyo, and Yumi in particular seem to recall memories that they've lost, through dreams. I wouldn't be surprised if most of the girls do, but then either forget them or think little of it. Blacking out also seems linked to past memories as well. At least that seems to be what Nodoka suggests.
Overall: The girls never really treated Sensei like he was just the creepy teacher that he is, in this timeline. This is likely due to their forgotten experiences with Senseis from past timelines.

New Maya seems to be the only example of a girl uninfluenced by their time in the resets.

Moonflare's Quiz: "Who Said This?" #01

Welcome to Moonflare's first ever quiz, named: "Who said this?". The rules are simple, you have to guess the character that said the following quotes without cheating. None of these quotes are from Akira, cause that'd be too difficult.

So, look at quote, guess who said it, check the answer to see if you got it right, move to the next one (while keeping track of your score). Let's go!
1: "Jesus, I wouldn't even be surprised if you had your fucking niece groomed already."
Yumi on "Fuck the Police".

2: "Does that mean you'll marry one?!"
Chinami on "Pool Party".

3: "So you've just been... wandering around all sad and lonely this whole time?"
Chika on "Dead in the Water".

4: "If you get good enough at ignoring something, it eventually feels like it's not even there."
Molly on "Ressurrection Sickness".

5: "First the roof, now this... Perhaps I should be the one checking on you instead?"
Makoto on "A Different View".

6: "I get to do whatever I want to you..."
Wakana on "Don't Hold Back".

7: "Congratulations on missing out on a chance for a free convenience store breakfast."
Maya on "Good Morning".

8: "Sensei, who is that really? And why do her eyes look like a cross between Ami's and Maya's?"
Noriko on "Eternity Until".

9: "You know, I've really gotta finish getting ready for the party now. So just... go ahead and do your own thing and we can talk, like... later. Or something."
Otoha on "Actual Jesus Quotes".

10: "Every pizza is a personal pizza if you try hard and believe in yourself."
Kaori on "Where the Trees Live".

Did you get them all? Maybe none? Was it too hard or too easy? Say something so I know if I should make this again sometime.

Moonflare's Quiz: "Who Said This?" #02

Okay, time for the second round. Hopefully this time it's balanced better and people will get more of them right. Rules are the same: it's all quotes from characters (excluding Akira) - and most of them are from popular moments in the game. Guess who said it, check the answer, move to the next one (while keeping track of your overall score).
I have also added a few more sentences from the same event to some of them, if I thought it was still too hard to guess (mind you, these sentences are not always the following sentence, but may be from a bit later in the event).

Lastly, for all the times I do this, the first line of the post will be the same to make it easier to search for them later.
Notice: Repeated characters are a possibility.

01: "Thanks for agreeing to hang out with me. Even though I probably just ruined the chances of that ever happening again." "I told myself I wouldn't cry but... holy shit, that was hard."
Rin in "Cry. Cry. Cry."

02: "You will like whatever I tell you to like and that's final." "Soft and sweet and full of cream! Happy hearts and hungry dreams! Cuteness turned up to extreme! Give this boy a MOE BEAM!!!"
Maya in "Misfit Maid Madness".

03: "You talk to birds. You are no authority on what does and doesn't make sense."
Himawari in "Ad Meliora".

04: "Well don't go blaming me for Sensei not wanting to dance on your little puppet strings anymore." "How do you expect him to grow if you won't let him?"
Noriko in "Goodnight".

05: "Just ask Maya what she thinks and go with that. You're just gonna side with her anyway."
Ami in "The first signs of fraying threads".

06: "Heheh... There are several answers to that question. Two of which are very naughty."
Yasu in "The cracking of the egg (nothing is beautiful)".

07: "It's really only my underwear and socks that bother me when they're wet and I already took those off like a minute ago."
Uta in "After the rain".

08: "Sensei... I... I can hear something... It's like... It's like... a ticking noise..."
Rin in "See you in the morning".

09: "Awwwww~ That's a really cute thing to say for someone who doesn't want to marry me yet." "You will. An angel told me."
Sara in "The place she falls asleep at night".

10: "I initially mistook them for a swinger couple trying to get the two of us involved in their... antics. And that this was a meeting designed to get me to open up to the idea of it."
Maya in "Lesbian stuff".

And there we go. Did this one go better? I look forward to your scores. I can make it even easier, but it's hard to not give it away, especially with popular events. Also, here's a silly bonus round for you all:
From "Brainrot LiL special": "Check your vibes, Arakawa. Let's get this ratioed."
Deadass Goth Chick Wakana.

Edit: I'll try to pace these more in the future, it's just now that I'm trying to get the formula right first.

Moonflare said:
You guessed it, it's time Moonflare ranted on why Himawari's name is Ami again. This will be kinda short (I tried guys) since it's just a new piece of information to add to the rest (there is a second one at the end though).

Okay so, basically, Himawari tells Akira to name her after his favorite flower. The obvious take from this is to guess that she's telling him to call her by the nickname "sunflower". Well, what she could actually be telling him is to call her Ami, since red hair Ami is his original sunflower, here's the evidence:

First Himawari tells him to call her after his favorite flower.
View attachment 3819739 View attachment 3819741 View attachment 3819742
Then we have confirmation she is his little sunflower.
View attachment 3819750 View attachment 3819751 View attachment 3819752
Well, Ami is also his sunflower.
View attachment 3819754 View attachment 3819755
Sunflower dress from Sekai.
View attachment 3819757
Now that we have established that both function as sunflowers, let's see them intersect. First of all, what is it the Akira has in his pocket? Well, it's a picture of Ami.
View attachment 3819758 View attachment 3819759
And do you know what else Akira has in his pocket? After their encounter at the church of New HOPE, in which there is the quiz, Himawari is the narrator outside of it. This bit establishes that it's her:
View attachment 3819770

then she explains that it isn't the knowledge that is dangerous, but your emotions when remembering. That's why her job is to always serve as a sunflower to Akira, taking the emotional damage off when he starts remembering stuff.
View attachment 3819777

I had to explain this for what happens next to make sense. As Akira leaves, still shaken from what he had seen, Himawari sends him a gift.
View attachment 3819781 View attachment 3819783 View attachment 3819784

Let's sum up, Himawari is a sunflower. Ami is also a sunflower. Akira carries a photo of Ami in his pocket. Himawari puts a photo of a sunflower in his pocket. When Akira asks what name he should give her, she says "name me after your favorite flower" - Ami is his favorite flower. Himawari wasn't telling him the secret of her nickname, she was telling him in a roundabout way what her actual name is. Again, alone, that might be stretching it but it's another thing on a huge pile of evidence.

And the other reason I thought to bring this up is that there is a dark undertone to Himawari being called Ami, and that is the possibility that Ami Arakawa dies at some point. It would be strange for Akira to have two daughters with the same name, or for them both to serve as his emotional support. Not impossible, but weird. If first Ami died though, it would make even more sense for them to honor her memory by giving their baby daughter her name. It would also explain Ami's obsession with asking people if they love Akira enough to die for him (cause she probably did).

Oh, and this is a minor thing, but I'm also adding it to the pile. Himawari is rambling on about stuff, and Ayane calls "Ami", to which she answers by shutting her mouth since her mother is calling her (and her big sister).

So far choices that cause you to miss events have all worked as you either pick right and unlock the event(s) or you pick a choice that makes you miss events.

Picking anyone other than Ayane will net you a couple lines of dialogue (at best) and no actual events. It's very unlikely that there'll be a Tsubasa threesome in future as a result of that event, as the game's been set up so far you can experience every event in one playthrough and that wouldn't be possible if you could pick either Tsubasa or Ayane in Mattress. If you want a green run, you have to pick Ayane.

If the Happy Scene is listed as '???' that just means you haven't seen it yet. If it's red, you've missed it either as the result of a choice you made - choosing not to engage in a sexual relationship with Ami will cause you to miss some Happy Scenes for example - or because the trigger was during a reset puzzle that you've already finished.

There are some you have to see to continue with the main events but aside from that if you missed any the only real effect (at the moment) is just that you didn't get to see the event and might not understand something you could've. I think.

posts.content_html_raw:
combige said:
Is there any risk to miss Tsubasa (theoretically, in the future) or Chinami event if I chose Ayane first?
Click to expand...
This addresses many recent posts. Selebus has stated, and reiterated quite a few times since then, that you can play the entire game without missing any event, which we call the "green path".

The walkthrough mod can guide you to achieve this most of the time (with a few minor exceptions, like not choosing to kill Kirin in the game, and choosing Miku as a winner in the costume competition - for which it could give better instructions).
Now, there are degrees to the green path. The broader green path is just about not missing events. So, in your example, you have to pick Ayane in "our time atop this mattress", because not doing so will lead to missing the threesome event.
There will be no other threesome event that comes from this decision, because that'd make it impossible for someone to get all events in a single playthrough. That's the logic.

Now, there are two other degrees to the green path. The middle one, which is where most of us stay, is picking everything that leads to significant content (not only events). For instance, choosing to trade nudes with Otoha leads to a difference in dialogue with Rin that is significant to the story (in the sense that it gives the stuff that follows more depth than otherwise), it just doesn't lead to events.
Another big one is choosing the Himawari option in "Scientific Research", which requires knowledge of what you're doing, and missing it will not alter the status of the event.
So, strictly speaking, you could choose not to do it and still have all events green - but we tend to add this to our idea of the green path.

Lastly, there's the green path almost no one takes - which is related to very insignificant stuff that won't make much of a difference, even though it is added content. For instance, Akira can be interested in furries, and that will be referenced later. Another one is naming Io's robot "1999 PC Classic, Rollercoaster Tycoon ", which will also get referenced later.
Most of these are, so far, inconsequential, although the name you give the baby could be consequential and we just don't know yet.

Fire Lord Zuko said:
Reason #2 - Allows You To Unlock Scenes/Events You Missed

Oh no! Looks like you made the wrong decision and now you missed an entire event in the game! Looks like you’re screwed unless you find another save or start the entire game over…

…is what I would say if the URM didn’t exist.

Let’s use a commonly missed event as an example: Rin’s “I Died With You” event from all the way back in Chapter 1:

View attachment 4139338

Well first of all, how did you miss it in the first place? What exactly happened? Here's a helpful bonus tip: there's an amazing wiki for this game that can really come in clutch when you need a quick refresher or tip on what to do. Except for the Reset Puzzles, but I'll get to that...

Anyway, regarding this Rin event, simply go to the Wiki, like so:

View attachment 4139217

Utilizing the nifty little search bar in the top right corner, type in the name of the event that you're missing. Or in this particular example, "I Died With You".

View attachment 4139218

Once on the event of your choosing, it's as simple as scrolling down and seeing why exactly you missed out on the event in the first place.

View attachment 4139219

Welp, looks like you were a Bad Homie to Rin... You kissed Chika before the Beach Vacation despite Rin telling you not to, didn't you? You scoundrel...

But that doesn't matter! Because with the URM, we can undo that mistake, and it will be as if it never happened! After all, who wants to beg for a save or play through the entire game all over again because of one mistake?

So how do you undo this mistake? Well, there's a helpful section on the wiki that can help with this too.

Scroll up until you see the section titled 'Technical Information'.

View attachment 4139220

Click on it and you should see another section titled 'Event Script Name'. That is our ticket to unlocking missed scenes in URM right there, and precisely what we need to type into our search bar.

View attachment 4139221

'cafe35'. Got it. Let's go back to the game and open URM.

View attachment 4139340

Right away, you'll see the variable is set to 'False', meaning that it never happened. To circumvent this, set it to 'True'.

View attachment 4139345

That should be it, right? Mission accomplished! Well, hold on... We still betrayed Rin, and technically shouldn't have this event to begin with because of it. What do we do about that? There's a variable for this too, which the game keeps track of.

Go back to your search bar and type in 'rinbetrayed'.

View attachment 4139343

Unlike the last one, this variable will be set to 'True', since, yes... we did betray Rin in this particular example. Simply set it to False.

View attachment 4139344

Congratulations! The once locked/missed Rin event will now be unlocked and fully accessible via the in-game replayer. Pretty useful, right?

View attachment 4139339
Click to expand...
It's like combige said. You'll want to change the variables of the missing events themselves, setting them from False to True, and also doing the opposite with any 'skip' variables you see (True to False). They're easy to spot if you're already searching for a specific event.

Moonflare said:
This addresses many recent posts. Selebus has stated, and reiterated quite a few times since then, that you can play the entire game without missing any event, which we call the "green path".

The walkthrough mod can guide you to achieve this most of the time (with a few minor exceptions, like not choosing to kill Kirin in the game, and choosing Miku as a winner in the costume competition - for which it could give better instructions).
Now, there are degrees to the green path. The broader green path is just about not missing events. So, in your example, you have to pick Ayane in "our time atop this mattress", because not doing so will lead to missing the threesome event.
View attachment 4742126 View attachment 4742130
There will be no other threesome event that comes from this decision, because that'd make it impossible for someone to get all events in a single playthrough. That's the logic.

Now, there are two other degrees to the green path. The middle one, which is where most of us stay, is picking everything that leads to significant content (not only events). For instance, choosing to trade nudes with Otoha leads to a difference in dialogue with Rin that is significant to the story (in the sense that it gives the stuff that follows more depth than otherwise), it just doesn't lead to events.
View attachment 4742124
Another big one is choosing the Himawari option in "Scientific Research", which requires knowledge of what you're doing, and missing it will not alter the status of the event.
View attachment 4742122
So, strictly speaking, you could choose not to do it and still have all events green - but we tend to add this to our idea of the green path.

Lastly, there's the green path almost no one takes - which is related to very insignificant stuff that won't make much of a difference, even though it is added content. For instance, Akira can be interested in furries, and that will be referenced later. Another one is naming Io's robot "1999 PC Classic, Rollercoaster Tycoon ", which will also get referenced later.
View attachment 4742138
Most of these are, so far, inconsequential, although the name you give the baby could be consequential and we just don't know yet.
Click to expand...
if you named the baby Ami you might be on the true green path

Although I share the frustration of having a month of FanFest, a minor delay for the next release, and the incoming break - I have always said that this is a place where we can both criticize and praise Selebus. And, this time, I don't share the overly judgemental view on him.

He wanted to spend an entire month goofing off with his own creation, he asked the people that pay him, and they gave him the "go for it". So, I mean, nothing wrong there. And the breaks themselves are planned.

I will say though that I agree that the timing is off. Were the Fanfest to become a thing, it would ideally be in the middle of the release cycle, not right before a break. (Fanfest -> seasonal content -> break) is an awful plan.
